policy: Initial JavaScript, desktop route and Settings ceilings were lowered after measured P2 reductions. Other reviewed ceilings remain unchanged. The PDF viewer feature ceiling rose from 500000 to 510000 for the PDF.js 6 security upgrade (GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j); the chunk loads only when a PDF is opened. Locale-only ceilings include the shared key dictionary and every canonical translated value. Further increases require a performance review. The 4.1.0 performance review adds exactly 9002 canonical locale bytes (0.461%) and 611 bytes to the largest catalog for four caption/reload labels in all 24 locales. Dictionary plus English grows 368 bytes; dictionary plus the largest selected catalog grows 744 bytes, with unchanged loading requests. JavaScript, CSS, route, feature and literal ceilings are unchanged. The Telegram API ToS rename (common.app_title becomes "Unofficial Telegram Drive") adds exactly 290 canonical locale bytes and 11 bytes to the largest catalog; nothing else changes. The Telegram API disclosure (common.telegram_api_notice, shown at sign-in, in the first-run introduction and in About) adds exactly 4053 canonical locale bytes and 319 bytes to the largest catalog, measured after the accurate-claims wording change; the locale ceilings are set to the measured totals. The desktop route grows 305 bytes for the shared notice component, so its ceiling rises 94 bytes to the measured size. Removing the built-in updater deletes the always-mounted update banner, the only initial-chunk user of framer-motion; the library now loads with the desktop route instead. Initial JavaScript falls from 504923 to 378375 bytes and its ceiling is lowered to that measured size; the desktop route rises from 302094 to 420791 bytes and its ceiling is set to that measured size; total JavaScript falls from 2453412 to 2439487 bytes. Dropping the update strings and adding the upstream credit line lowers the locale data to 1945580 canonical bytes and 138278 bytes for the largest catalog; both ceilings are lowered to those measured sizes. The Telegram-session-at-rest security change (session unlock, passphrase setup and keychain-unavailable screens) adds 21 strings in all 24 locales. Built on top of the ad and supporter removal it adds 36067 bytes of locale data (1632437 to 1668504) and 2538 bytes to the largest catalog (115341 to 117879); the locale ceilings rise by the reviewed 35797 and 2455 bytes to 1981377 and 140733, which still leaves headroom above the measured sizes. The session check and unlock screen add 148 bytes to initial JavaScript, so its ceiling rises from 378375 to the measured 378523; CSS, route and feature ceilings are unchanged. The option to remove a keychain-sealed session when the credential store is unreachable adds 2 strings in all 24 locales (within the locale ceilings) and 270 bytes to initial JavaScript, so its ceiling rises from 378523 to the measured 378793. Rebasing onto main after the code-quality changes (#40-#42) measures initial JavaScript at 378942 bytes (+149 from the combined tree), so its ceiling is set to that measured size.
